Building heights come from OpenStreetMap level counts where given; elsewhere we estimated them from the building's type and footprint – hover over a building to see which. Trees were identified from the Meta / WRI 1 m canopy-height map made from satellite imagery. The map placed the canopies well but greatly underestimated their heights, so we corrected the heights from our photos taken from the roof; the tall, narrow trees north of Building O were redrawn by hand. The same photos refined the massing of the Polinszky Auditorium, the pitched roofs on Wartha Vince utca and the two car parks; the roof shapes of twelve more neighbouring houses were modelled from satellite imagery.

The youngest part of the city. Nearly half of Egyetemváros's residents are aged 15–39. On a teaching day about 1,700 students live in the zone, and roughly another 2,000 arrive from other parts of the city and 17 surrounding settlements. [1] [5] [11]

html.\u003cb\u003eHiányzó közösségi tér.\u003: Missing community space. Despite all these people, there is only one community place within 500 m of Building O: Pannon KözTér, on the ground floor of the University of Pannonia's Building E since 2021, part of the European Capital of Culture programme. There is no public square or pedestrian street, and no market. A circle of the same size around Óváros tér holds 19 cultural and community institutions and 7 squares. [12] [13]

html.Tanítási napokon kb. 1\u0026nbsp;700 hal: On teaching days about 1,700 students live in the 15-minute zone, about 18% of the zone's daytime population. According to the census, 2,401 Veszprém residents are in higher education, yet 4,440 students were enrolled at the University of Pannonia's Veszprém sites (autumn 2021/22). That is nearly twice as many, so a large share of the students come from elsewhere. [3] [4] [11]
